claims.explanation: NSC-663284 is a quinone-based Cdc25 inhibitor that also redox cycles to generate reactive oxygen species, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on Cdc25A/B/C for cell-cycle progression combined with sensitivity to oxidative stress. Tumors with high Cdc25 expression or KEAP1/NFE2L2 mutations that impair antioxidant responses are expected to be more sensitive, while intact antioxidant capacity or low Cdc25 expression may protect.

features.basis: NSC-663284 directly inhibits Cdc25A (Ki 29 nM) and blocks Cdk2 activation; high expression increases dependence
NSC-663284 is most selective for Cdc25B (Ki 95 nM) and inhibits it in cells; high expression increases dependence
NSC-663284 inhibits Cdc25C (Ki 89 nM) and causes G2/M arrest; high expression increases dependence
Damaging KEAP1 mutations impair NRF2 degradation and antioxidant response, increasing sensitivity to redox-cycling quinone
Activating NFE2L2 mutations may paradoxically sensitize to oxidative stress by altering redox balance, as seen in HEC265
Cdc25 inhibition blocks Cdk1 activation; high cyclin B1 reflects G2/M dependence and sensitivity
Cdc25 inhibitors block dephosphorylation and activation of Cdk1; high Cdk1 activity increases dependence
Cdc25A activates Cdk2/cyclin A; high cyclin A indicates dependence on Cdc25A for S/G2 progression
Cdc25A reactivates Cdk2/cyclin A; high Cdk2 increases dependence on Cdc25A
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so not a strong predictor; may allow survival in some contexts
BRAF mutations appear enriched in sensitive melanoma and other lines, possibly via MAPK-driven proliferation
PTEN loss occurs in several sensitive lines and may increase dependence on Cdc25 for proliferation
